title: What did the stars teach us?
old_caption: Graduation day for the stars. The biggest lesson: a chart can describe you, but it never decides for you. You're a whole chart and a whole person. Go love well.

title: Red flag or green flag?
old_caption: No sign is a red flag. Behavior is. Green looks like consistency, respecting a no and real curiosity about you. Watch what people do, not their birthday.

title: How do you end things kindly?
old_caption:
Being "busy this week" for a month leaves a door half open. Ending things kindly means being clear, brief and warm.
Kind isn't the same as vague. Close the door gently.

title: What are the 12 houses?
old_caption:
Astrologers split a chart into 12 houses, each one an area of life, starting from your rising sign. Planet is the what, sign is the how, house is the where.
Every planet gets its own room.

title: Where does jealousy come from?
old_caption: Jealousy is a normal feeling, and it usually points to a fear or a need underneath. Talk about the need instead of policing the person. Name it, gently, and don't aim it.

title: Who is Juno in astrology?
old_caption:
Juno is an asteroid in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter, found in 1804. Some astrologers read it as commitment and partnership.
If a space rock can commit, so can you, when it feels right.

title: What keeps love lasting?
old_caption: Lasting love isn't fireworks. It's small daily attention, staying curious, saying thank you and repairing after fights. Sometimes it's just a cup of tea brought without asking.

title: Is astrology a science?
old_caption:
Is astrology a science? Astronomy is the science of the sky. Astrology is a symbolic tradition many people use to reflect and talk.
Use it to ask better questions, never to decide for you.

title: How do you actually listen?
old_caption: Want to really listen? Reflect back what you heard, ask one question, and wait before you jump in to fix it. Most people want to feel heard first.

title: What's love bombing?
old_caption:
"Soulmate" on day two and nonstop gifts can feel dazzling. Big romance isn't the problem; intensity that later turns into pressure is.
Real interest goes at your pace. If it's real, it'll still be real next week.
